review_scope: Clause 20/21 ASN.1 framing tranche: a single shared BACnetTimeStamp codec (bare CHOICE + wrapped forms, sequence-number range enforced in both directions), full Clause 21 framing of BACnetEventParameter, BACnetFaultParameter, BACnetPropertyStates, BACnetDeviceObjectPropertyReference, BACnetRecipient, and BACnetAddress driving Event_Parameters/Fault_Parameters/Recipient_List property reads and writes, the GetEventInformation-ACK bare-timestamp migration, plus review hardening (trailing-bytes rejection, fixed-width bit-string validation, strict stored-list routing). Conventions unchanged: `repo_sha` names the tip of the PR branch `codex/encoding-asn1-framing` at the time of writing (the last code commit; this docs-refresh commit lands after it), matching how `e6be3eac` was recorded for the previous tranche.
addenda_errata_status: Local source `_spec/2020_ASHRAE_Standard-135-BACnet-Data-Communication-Protocol.pdf` was reviewed for the Clause 20.2.1 tag-form rules, the cited Clause 21 productions, Clause 12.12/12.21 + Table 12-25, and Annex K.2.25. No external addenda/errata check was performed for this tranche; per-row scope is recorded in each row's notes.

rows.requirement_summary: Server transaction state machine behavior, segmented request handling, SegmentACK behavior, and abort/reject mapping.
rows.notes: This slice adds server segmented ComplexAck send-side SegmentACK validation: SegmentACKs with the server bit set are ignored, positive ACKs advance only for the current segment, negative ACKs retransmit only the current requested segment, out-of-range negative ACKs are ignored, stale final ACKs do not complete the transfer, timeout retries retransmit before idle cleanup without a final timeout Abort, client Abort is routed to terminate the active segmented response without a spurious timeout Abort, routed SegmentACK/Abort events match the NPDU source-network key, segmented response frames set NPDU expecting_reply while waiting for SegmentACK, dispatch filters stale/future ACKs before queue insertion and does not block on a full SegmentACK queue, client Abort and same-peer/invoke-id replacement use nonblocking control events, live segmented sender tasks are capped by permits until each task exits, and replacement cancels the older sender so it cannot later emit a timeout Abort. The row remains below supported status pending a fuller server TSM transition audit, configured APDU segment timeout/retry exposure, and broader Reject/Error failure mapping coverage.

rows.requirement_summary: Only Confirmed-Request and ComplexACK may be segmented; SegmentACK windows and modulo-256 sequence handling are enforced.
rows.notes: This slice adds server ComplexAck send-side window evidence for current-sequence positive ACK advancement, first-window NAK0 retransmission, NAK of the previous sequence retransmitting the current segment, stale/future positive ACK ignore, wrong-direction ACK ignore, routed source-network matching, out-of-range NAK ignore, final ACK validation, timeout retransmission, repeated valid NAK abort, ACK flood/current-window filtering, and nonblocking full-queue SegmentACK dispatch. Remaining segmentation/window gaps include multi-segment window sizes beyond the current window-one send behavior, modulo-256 wrap, duplicate segment receive behavior, max APDU/max segment boundaries, and broader client/server receive-side out-of-order coverage.

rows.requirement_summary: Notification Class Recipient_List reads and writes use the Clause 21 BACnetDestination framing: seven application-tagged members in order (valid-days BACnetDaysOfWeek, from-time, to-time, recipient, process-identifier, issue-confirmed-notifications, transitions) concatenated as a BACnetLIST, with BACnetRecipient discriminated by context tag (device [0] primitive ObjectIdentifier, address [1] constructed BACnetAddress of application Unsigned16 + OCTET STRING).
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL; scope is the modeled NotificationClass path (NotificationForwarder's Recipient_List is a stub today). Golden vectors cover the device, address (nonzero network), and broadcast (zero-length MAC) forms; the 8-entry list round-trip covers the Annex K.2.25 AE-CRL-B minimum-entries posture. Decode is strict end to end: element sequence, fixed-width bit-string members (exactly one content octet with unused_bits 1 for valid-days / 5 for transitions), and whole-list routing (a malformed stored list fails closed with no prefix delivery). The write path and the routing filter share one flat-entry decoder, and the pre-#152 flat application-tagged form remains accepted there as a compatibility fallback. Indexed writes are rejected (Tranche K / #260 family). Remaining work: interop evidence against a second implementation and NotificationForwarder Recipient_List modeling.

rows.requirement_summary: Event_Parameters and Fault_Parameters read/write use the full Clause 21 ASN.1 CHOICE framing of BACnetEventParameter and BACnetFaultParameter: alternatives over SEQUENCEs as opening/closing context tag pairs with context-tagged members, explicitly tagged inner CHOICEs, fault-out-of-range inner CHOICEs discovered by application tag, and BACnetPropertyStates elements with the 135-2020 CHOICE tags.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL. Evidence covers the modeled alternatives (change-of-bitstring/change-of-state/change-of-value/floating-limit/out-of-range/extended; all eight fault parameters) with golden vectors and round-trips, Opaque preservation of unmodeled alternatives (byte-for-byte for constructed forms; none [20] NULL decodes to Opaque{20, []} and re-encodes constructed), rejection of omitted/deprecated/reserved tags 6/7/12/19, rejection of trailing garbage after a framed element, property-state goldens, and the legacy flat + OctetString-to-Opaque write fallback retained per #129; unmodeled Opaques never reach the legacy little-endian evaluator. The framed property-state codec uses 135-2020 CHOICE tags which correct invented pre-2020 tags for door/timer/lift variants; the older BACnetNotificationParameters codec in bacnet-services still uses the old tags for those variants -- reconciling it is follow-up work with its own wire change (out of this row's scope).

Issue #83 evidence adds SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple request lifetime encoding/decoding in the standard field order, mandatory issue-confirmed validation, paired lifetime/max-delay validation, cancellation handling for empty contexts and listed property specs, context lifetime refresh, and server-side subscription expiration from the decoded lifetime. This row remains below supported status until fuller BIBB/PICS and clause-level conformance evidence exists, including first-failed-subscription response shape, complete Device active-COV property synchronization, context-level Active_COV_Multiple_Subscriptions evidence, and fuller clause-level evidence.

rows.requirement_summary: All BACnetTimeStamp producers and consumers share one codec: time [0] as a primitive context tag 0 of length 4 holding raw Time octets, sequence-number [1] constrained to Unsigned (0..65535) and enforced on encode and decode, datetime [2] as an opening/closing tag 2 pair around application-tagged Date and Time, in both bare-CHOICE (SEQUENCE OF member) and field-wrapped forms.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-21-FORMAL-APDUS. Resolves the divergent dual-codec defect from #259 per the Clause 20.2.1 tag-form rules: time [0] tags the primitive base type Time, so the primitives codec's primitive-tag form is conformant and the GetEventInformationAck opening-tag-0 form was removed. Golden vectors, 0/65535 boundary acceptance, 65536 and 3-octet overflow rejection, and a cross-call-site primitives<->GetEventInformationAck matrix all run in-tree.

rows.requirement_summary: Original-Unicast-NPDU frames preserve exact BVLC length, payload validation, and source/reply semantics.
rows.notes: Generic BVLL envelope coverage exists. J-04 Original-NPDU evidence covers UDP sender B/IP MAC delivery to the upper layer and self-originated frame suppression. Directed reply-path integration remains open.

rows.requirement_summary: Original-Broadcast-NPDU frames are encoded, decoded, and routed according to BACnet/IP broadcast semantics.
rows.notes: Generic BVLL envelope coverage exists. J-04 Original-NPDU evidence covers BBMD handling of Original-Broadcast-NPDU: local delivery uses sender B/IP MAC, remote BDT peer and registered FDT targets receive Forwarded-NPDU with the original sender encoded, and the BBMD does not echo the already-local broadcast back onto the local subnet as Forwarded-NPDU. J-09 adds platform socket evidence for Annex J local broadcast prerequisites: the B/IP socket binds INADDR_ANY for subnet/limited-broadcast reception while retaining the configured interface in the local B/IP MAC, and SO_BROADCAST is enabled for Original-Broadcast-NPDU sends. J-10 adds B/IP send-path evidence that Clause 6 global-broadcast and remote-broadcast NPDUs preserve DNET, DLEN 0 broadcast DADR, Hop Count, and APDU bytes unchanged inside Annex J Original-Broadcast-NPDU. Additional malformed/unsupported-path coverage remains open.

rows.requirement_summary: Forwarded-NPDU includes a valid originating BACnet/IP MAC and preserves source-address semantics.
rows.notes: J-04 covers generic originating-address parsing, truncated-address rejection, BBMD delivery with originating B/IP source MAC, FDT fanout preserving the origin, local rebroadcast for unicast peer arrivals, directed-broadcast peer local-rebroadcast suppression, and no onward forwarding to other BDT peers. Original-Broadcast fanout covers BDT/FDT Forwarded-NPDU emission with original sender preservation and no local echoed Forwarded-NPDU. Non-BDT Forwarded-NPDU evidence verifies rejection before local delivery, local rebroadcast, BDT fanout, or FDT fanout. DBTN evidence covers registered foreign-device fanout to local broadcast, BDT peer, and non-origin FDT peer while preserving the origin, excluding origin echo, checking for no extra duplicate frames, and returning X'0060' when deterministic local Forwarded-NPDU forwarding fails.

rows.requirement_summary: BBMD Broadcast Distribution Table write/read/ACK behavior and peer broadcast fanout are validated.
rows.notes: J-03 covers read/write BDT caller paths, replacement semantics, malformed Write-BDT NAK without table mutation, self-entry insertion without overflow, and directed-broadcast forwarding target calculation. J-04 adds Forwarded-NPDU BDT mask behavior: full-mask peers require local rebroadcast, directed-broadcast and unknown peers skip it, Forwarded-NPDUs are not forwarded onward to other BDT peers, and non-BDT senders are rejected before BDT fanout. Original-Broadcast fanout covers one remote BDT target and verifies no local Forwarded-NPDU echo. DBTN fanout covers a registered foreign-device request forwarded to a BDT peer plus local broadcast and FDT targets without extra duplicate frames. J-07 adds project ACL evidence for the legacy Write-BDT path: listed management senders can update the table, and unlisted senders receive the standard Write-BDT NAK without table mutation. J-08 adds BDT persistence evidence: successful Write-BDT stores the current wire-format BDT for restart load, and invalid persisted bytes fall back to the configured BDT without accepting malformed state. J-11 adds client-side Read-Broadcast-Distribution-Table-Ack validation that rejects malformed payload lengths not divisible by the Annex J.2.4 N*10 BDT entry size. J-12 adds raw BBMD Read-Broadcast-Distribution-Table-Ack wire evidence for ACK function code and N*10 BDT entry bytes. J-13 adds reproducible BBMD stress benchmark A/B runner evidence with ignored raw artifacts and a machine-readable result-row schema.

rows.requirement_summary: Foreign-device registration, TTL bounds, re-registration, read/delete FDT, expiry, and DBTN authorization are validated.
rows.notes: J-03 covers FDT read/register/delete caller paths, re-registration, zero-TTL and malformed TTL NAKs, exact Delete-FDT payload length, max TTL remaining-time capping, expiry purge, source exclusion, and unregistered DBTN NAK without local delivery. J-04 Original-Broadcast evidence covers fanout to one registered foreign device while preserving the original sender in the Forwarded-NPDU. DBTN evidence covers registered origin plus peer FDT fanout, preserves the original foreign-device B/IP source, verifies no echo to the originating foreign device, checks for no extra duplicate FDT frames, and verifies a registered origin receives X'0060' when forwarding cannot be completed. Non-BDT Forwarded-NPDU evidence verifies no FDT fanout. J-06 adds a BBMD-owned timer purge task for Annex J.5.2.3, covers expiration without an inbound BVLC request, and covers re-registration resetting the entry before the purge task removes it. J-07 adds project ACL evidence for Delete-FDT: listed management senders can delete registered entries, and unlisted senders receive the standard Delete-FDT NAK without removing the entry. J-11 adds client-side Read-Foreign-Device-Table-Ack validation that rejects malformed payload lengths not divisible by the Annex J.2.8 N*10 FDT entry size. J-12 adds raw BBMD Read-Foreign-Device-Table-Ack wire evidence for ACK function code and N*10 FDT entry fields. J-13 adds reproducible foreign-device/BBMD stress benchmark A/B runner evidence with ignored raw artifacts and a machine-readable result-row schema.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC BVLC-SC frame function, control, options, VMAC, and payload validation.
rows.notes: AB-01 adds transport codec evidence for Annex AB.2 control flag bits 7..4 rejection, Header Option Type 1..31 enforcement, AB.2.17 destination/data option marker decoding, VMAC field ordering, option count cap enforcement, option length truncation, option data truncation, and unterminated option-chain rejection. Addenda 135-2020cf/cp were checked for this row: cf renames Data Options bit 6 to Every Segment without changing the marker bit position, and cp adds standard header option types 2..5 that remain accepted by the generic 1..31 parser. Broader non-Result BVLC-SC function-specific payload semantics, destination-option Must Understand NAK behavior, Every Segment segmentation behavior, and hub/direct-connection behavior remain for later Annex AB work.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC BVLC-Result ACK/NAK payload parsing and connection handling.
rows.notes: AB-02 adds typed BVLC-Result ACK/NAK payload parsing for transport. ACK fixtures use the Proprietary-Message function per addendum 135-2020ci, while NAK fixtures mirror AB.2.17 examples with and without UTF-8 Error Details, including the Figure AB-6 multibyte UTF-8 details bytes. Negative evidence covers ACK trailing fields, short NAKs, unknown result codes, invalid UTF-8 details, malformed empty payloads, Data Options absence, Connect-Request NAK failing before timeout, fatal Result NAK closing the receive loop before further heartbeats, and malformed wire-level Result decode failures closing without a Result response. Transport connection handling now keeps ACK benign, disconnects on NAK, and disconnects on malformed Result without generating a Result response. Negotiated Max-BVLC-Length resource-limit evidence is tracked under BACNET-AB-SC-CONNECTION-STATE. Remaining work includes request correlation, Error Details resource limits, standard-function ACK diagnostic policy, BVLC-Result generation for every AB.3.1.5 error situation, destination-option Must Understand NAK behavior, and hub/direct response-routing behavior.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC Data Options are exposed to the network layer as data_attributes and handled explicitly across supported SC/non-SC boundaries.
rows.notes: This row now has native receive-side, outbound send, router local-delivery, router forwarding, and unsupported Must Understand fail-closed evidence for BACnet/SC Encapsulated-NPDU Data Options. Receive paths convert supported or non-Must-Understand Data Options into generic transport DataAttribute values, preserving option type, Must Understand flag, and option data on ReceivedNpdu; NetworkLayer exposes those attributes on ReceivedApdu after NPDU decode; router local-delivery paths retain inbound attributes; router forwarding attaches inbound attributes to forwarded unicast and broadcast SendRequest values; and non-SC transports emit empty data_attributes on receive. Native SC treats valid Secure Path Data Option type 1 as understood, rejects other Must Understand Data Options before NPDU delivery, returns BVLC-Result NAK COMMUNICATION/HEADER_NOT_UNDERSTOOD with the offending option marker for non-broadcast traffic, drops broadcast traffic without a result, and preserves unsupported non-Must-Understand Data Options as DataAttribute values. Outbound paths add attribute-aware TransportPort and NetworkLayer send helpers, keep non-SC transports on default ignore-on-send behavior, and encode SC DataAttribute values as Data Options while validating option type 1..31, the 64-option cap, and u16 option-data lengths before writing the BVLC-SC frame. Router tests cover forwarded unicast, forwarded broadcast, and loopback SC-to-SC forwarding preserving Data Options on the outbound SC frame. Remaining work is native send-path enforcement of the Secure Path type-1 marker constraints (to_data_options accepts a type-1 option without Must Understand and with a payload; the only prior evidence for those constraints was a removed non-native build path), high-level helper address-resolution/target-VMAC behavior, and formal conformance-test evidence.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC initiating and accepting peers enforce connection-state transitions, Connect-Accept response correlation, disconnect final-message behavior, and duplicate-VMAC collision signaling.
rows.notes: AB-03 adds native Connect-Accept message-id matching evidence, preserves the Connecting state when a pure state-machine response does not match the pending Connect-Request, and makes the async native handshake fail/disconnect on a mismatched response. Native Connect-Accept handling now requires the fixed AB.2.11.1 26-byte payload before entering Connected, stores peer Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length, advertises local Max-BVLC-Length, rejects outbound NPDUs or encoded BVLC frames that exceed peer limits, and discards oversized inbound WebSocket payloads before BVLC processing. The hub stores client Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length from Connect-Request, advertises its own limits in Connect-Accept, rejects non-26-byte Connect-Request payloads, drops inbound frames above the hub limit before decode, and filters unicast/broadcast relay targets by each recipient's negotiated NPDU and encoded BVLC limits. The hub BVLC-Result NAK builder now takes typed BACnet ErrorClass/ErrorCode values; duplicate client or hub VMAC collisions are encoded as COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151) instead of raw 1/1, and known-but-invalid functions are no longer classified as BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN. AB-07 stores each hub client's Device UUID, accepts known-UUID Connect-Request replacements, sends a WebSocket Close to the superseded connection, wakes the superseded handler, keeps superseded sinks from relaying or removing the replacement entry, and revalidates both source and recipient closed tokens immediately before relay writes so marked-superseded sinks are not written after replacement wins. It also preserves NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC NAK behavior for a new UUID that collides with an existing client or hub VMAC. Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence now requires the superseded connection to receive a Close frame, rejects a second Connect-Request from an already connected client without replacing a peer that it claims, verifies the closed client's original VMAC is no longer reachable, verifies peer reachability after that invalid connected-state transition, and decodes duplicate-VMAC BVLC-Result NAK values at the WebSocket boundary. Transport receive-loop evidence now covers WebSocket close/error receive paths transitioning the native connection to Disconnected before exit, heartbeat send failures disconnecting before retry/exit, reconnect exhaustion leaving Disconnected, and oversized frame discard. Existing transport tests also cover connect timeout to Disconnected, Disconnect-Request construction, Disconnect-ACK transition from Disconnecting, and hub Device UUID payload parsing. This tranche adds Annex H.7.3 Random-48 VMAC generation, native Connect-Request BVLC-Result handling that detects COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151), requires the BVLC-Result message ID to match the pending Connect-Request before reseeding, disconnects, clears the pending connect, and installs a new Random-48 VMAC before later attempts. Native duplicate-VMAC reseed failure now blocks failover/retry eligibility so a stale duplicate VMAC is not sent on a subsequent failover Connect-Request. Failed primary-restore probes now copy a successful Random-48 reseed or fail-closed retry-block state back to the active connection before the probe is discarded, preventing later primary-restore or reconnect attempts from reusing a stale duplicate VMAC. Native connect-time failures now clear the pending Connect-Request on timeouts, invalid Connect-Accept responses, malformed BVLC-Result wires, generic SC decode errors, and WebSocket send/receive I/O errors. It also adds failover and primary-restore evidence that retry Connect-Requests use the reselected VMAC, primary-restore reseed-failure evidence that no stale-VMAC retry is sent, generic and wrong-message-id Connect-Request NAK evidence that does not reseed. Remaining AB.6.2 gaps include explicit AWAITING_WEBSOCKET modeling at the WebSocket adapter boundary, accepting-peer connect-wait timeout, Disconnect wait behavior in ScTransport::stop, and reserved VMAC error signaling.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC hub connector, hub relay behavior, VMAC routing, disconnect, and failover behavior are validated.
rows.notes: AB-06 adds hub connector/forwarding evidence for Annex AB.5.3.2, AB.5.3.3, and AB.5.4. Hub-bound Encapsulated-NPDU messages now carry Destination Virtual Address and omit Originating Virtual Address; local receive logic accepts hub-relayed unicast with no Destination Virtual Address and drops non-broadcast Destination Virtual Address from hub relay. The hub rejects forwarding attempts with an Originating Virtual Address or missing Destination Virtual Address, selects only the matching VMAC for unicast, discards unknown unicast destinations by producing no recipient, fans broadcast to all current hub connections except the origin, preserves Message ID/payload/destination options/data options, adds the sender Originating Virtual Address, strips Destination Virtual Address for unicast forwarding, and preserves broadcast Destination Virtual Address for broadcast forwarding. Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence covers three connected clients: A-to-B unicast reaches only B with the required VMAC transformation and option preservation, A-to-unknown unicast reaches no client, and A broadcast reaches B and C but not A while preserving the broadcast Destination Virtual Address. AB-07 adds live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence that a known Device UUID replacement moves hub reachability to the replacement VMAC, prevents old-VMAC unicast delivery, requires a Close frame for the superseded connection, prevents marked-superseded source or recipient sinks from relaying after replacement wins, and preserves peer reachability after rejecting a connected client's second Connect-Request. Transport connector evidence now covers initial primary timeout to failover, established primary loss with reconnect exhaustion, failover Connect-Request/Connect-Accept, connection state update, active unicast send-path swap to the failover hub, and primary restoration while failover is active. Primary restoration uses a separate probe connection, sends a best-effort Disconnect-Request to the failover hub after the primary Connect-Accept succeeds, swaps the active transport path back to the primary hub, and verifies subsequent unicast traffic is sent to the restored primary. This slice adds relay helper and live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence that 31 minimum-size Destination Options plus 31 minimum-size Data Options remain within the 1476-byte BVLC size budget and are preserved through hub unicast relay; helper coverage also verifies broadcast preservation with the same option chains. This slice also adds explicit unsupported direct-connection classification evidence: the hub WebSocket subprotocol selection rejects `dc.bsc.bacnet.org`, and a connected hub client sending Address-Resolution receives a BVLC-Result NAK with COMMUNICATION/UNEXPECTED_DATA rather than BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN. Configured hub URI evidence covers the production TlsWebSocket::connect parse boundary preserving the configured wss authority, port, path, and query before dialing; malformed or hostless configured hub URIs are rejected before any WebSocket/TLS dial. ASHRAE Addendum cc to 135-2020 changes AB.5.3.1 hub-connection metadata and Network Port properties but does not change these forwarding, replacement, reconnect-failover, option-preservation, configured/malformed hub URI, or direct-connection unsupported-classification behaviors. No remaining hub connector gaps are tracked in this row.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC WebSocket subprotocol, binary frames, wss/TLS, TLS 1.3, and mutual TLS expectations are enforced or explicitly limited.
rows.notes: AB-04 adds native WebSocket evidence for configured-peer URI scheme rejection before dialing unless the scheme is wss, native initiating-peer verification that the selected hub subprotocol is hub.bsc.bacnet.org, accepting-hub rejection of missing/wrong subprotocol offers, successful real TLS WebSocket hub subprotocol negotiation, and real TLS WebSocket text-frame close with status 1003. Native and hub adapters already send BVLC-SC payloads as binary WebSocket frames and ignore Ping/Pong as optional WebSocket control traffic. AB-05 adds TLS 1.3-only native Python hub configuration, TLS 1.3-only benchmark/test helper configuration, generated-certificate evidence for valid mTLS, missing client certificate, wrong client issuer, expired/not-yet-valid client and server certificates, wrong server SAN, malformed PEM, mismatched cert/key pairs, explicit TLS 1.3 negotiation, and TLS 1.2-only client rejection. The benchmark SC hub now enforces client certificates when --ca is supplied. Direct WebSocket connections using dc.bsc.bacnet.org remain deferred/unsupported because direct connections are not implemented or publicly claimed. The combined AB.7 row remains implementation-present-needs-security-tests until TLS 1.3 application profile/cipher-suite evidence, revocation behavior when configured, production file-path helper tests, and any optional certificate identity policy are fully evidenced; server-auth-only examples remain documented as non-conformant example/benchmark mode.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC heartbeat request/ack behavior, timeout range, disconnect, and retry behavior are validated.
rows.notes: AB.6.3 heartbeat evidence now covers no-VMAC Heartbeat-Request/Heartbeat-ACK construction, native Heartbeat-ACK message-id/no-VMAC validation, production `ScTransport::start` rejection of configurable heartbeat intervals outside 3..300 seconds, production rejection of disconnect timeouts that are not greater than the heartbeat interval, periodic heartbeat initiation after idle inbound BVLC activity, inbound BVLC activity resetting the liveness timer, timeout-driven native disconnect when no BVLC response arrives, send-error disconnect behavior, and hub-initiated heartbeat tracking that sends idle Heartbeat-Requests, records the pending Message ID, clears the pending state only for a matching Heartbeat-ACK, and removes the hub client when the pending ACK exceeds the hub timeout. Accelerated native heartbeat tests use a private test-only timing override so production builders keep Annex AB.6.3 range enforcement at start. The row remains open because the native heartbeat timeout evidence relies on a test-only timing override rather than formal Annex AB.6.3 timeout conformance tests.
